data-truncate-words='70'> <p class="strong tightBot">Application</p> <p class='applicationDetails noMargVert notranslate'>I applied online. The process took a week. I interviewed at <tt class='i-emp'>Jane Street</tt>.</p> <p class="strong tightBot">Interview</p> <p class='interviewDetails noMargTop notranslate truncateThis'>Email from HR to schedule phone interview. Phone interview with QR from Jane Street a few days later. Overall the interview was very difficult, but the researcher was very friendly and helped through the process when I was stuck. Some difficult probability questions. Questions like these are easy once you see them, but difficult when you first try them. I&#039;d recommend getting exposure to as many questions as possible.</p> <p class="strong tightVert">Interview Questions</p> <div class='interviewQuestions margBot notranslate'> <ul class='undecorated'> <li> <span class='interviewQuestion noPadVert truncateThis ' data-truncate-words='70'>Given deck of cards A and deck of cards B, which deck would you rather choose from if you need to choose two cards of the same color on consecutive draws? Deck A is a normal 52 card deck, Deck B is a 26 card deck with 50% black and 50% red. What if we add deck C, which is a 26 card deck that comes from a random subset of deck A? &nbsp;</span> <a href="/Interview/Given-deck-of-cards-A-and-deck-of-cards-B-which-deck-would-you-rather-choose-from-if-you-need-to-choose-two-cards-of-the-s-QTN_1210428.htm" class="questionResponse">1 Answer</a></li> <li> <span class='interviewQuestion noPadVert truncateThis ' data-truncate-words='70'>You play rock, paper, scissors with an opponent, but your opponent cannot play rock. What should you play to maximize your expected profit if every time you win you win $1, lose you lose $1, draw you win $0? &nbsp;</span> <a href="/Interview/You-play-rock-paper-scissors-with-an-opponent-but-your-opponent-cannot-play-rock-What-should-you-play-to-maximize-your-QTN_1210429.htm" class="questionResponse">1 Answer</a></li> <li> <span class='interviewQuestion noPadVert truncateThis ' data-truncate-words='70'>Play rock, paper, scissors again and again your opponent cannot throw rock. The game ends when one person loses. You play another round if there is a draw. What is your strategy? &nbsp;</span> <a href="/Interview/Play-rock-paper-scissors-again-and-again-your-opponent-cannot-throw-rock-The-game-ends-when-one-person-loses-You-play-a-QTN_1210430.htm" class="questionResponse">1 Answer</a></li> </ul> </div> </div> <span class='hidden'> <span class="item"> <span class="fn i-emp"> Jane Street</span> </span> <span class='dtreviewed notranslate'> data-truncate-toggle='true' data-truncate-words='70'> <p class="strong tightBot">Application</p> <p class='applicationDetails noMargVert notranslate'>I applied online. The process took a week. I interviewed at <tt class='i-emp'>Jane Street</tt> (New York, NY).</p> <p class="strong tightBot">Interview</p> <p class='interviewDetails noMargTop notranslate truncateThis'>Applied online. Quick response time. Set up a phone interview with a researcher before HR briefing (a pleasant surprise). I was shocked at the nature (basic nature that is, is this the flavor of problems they tackle at Jane street????) of questions I was being tested on (not that I got them right....) They want you to assess how well you can quantify your confidence in the answer you give them.</p> <p class="strong tightVert">Interview Questions</p> <div class='interviewQuestions margBot notranslate'> <ul class='undecorated'> <li> <span class='interviewQuestion noPadVert truncateThis ' data-truncate-words='70'>Interesting question: From a deck of 52 cards pick 26 at random. </p> </div> <div class='tbl fill padTop'> <div class='row'> <div class='cell sqLogoCell showDesk'> <span class='sqLogo tighten smSqLogo logoOverlay'> <img data-original='https://media.glassdoor.com/sqls/255549/jane-street-squarelogo-1384201197714.png' data-original-2x='https://media.glassdoor.com/sqlm/255549/jane-street-squarelogo-1384201197714.png' src='' class='notranslate_alt notranslate_title lazy' data-retina-ok='true' alt='' title=''/> </span> </div> <div class='cell'> <h2 class='summary strong noMargTop tightTop'> <span class='reviewer'>Quantitative Researcher</span> Interview</h2> <div class='tbl reviewMeta notranslate'> <div class='cell middle'> <div class='author minor'> Anonymous Interview Candidate</div> </div> </div> </div> </div> </div> <div class='tbl fill padTopSm'> <div class='row'> <div class='cell sqLogoCell showDesk'></div> <div class='cell reviewBodyCell'> <div class='interviewOutcomes'> <div class='flex-grid'> <div class='tightLt col span-1-3'> <div class='middle'> <div class="cell"><i class='sqLed middle sm red margRtSm '></i> </div><div class="cell"><span class='middle'>No Offer</span> </div></div></div> <div class='tightLt col span-1-3'> <div class='middle'> <div class="cell"><i class='sqLed middle sm yellow margRtSm '></i> </div><div class="cell"><span class='middle'>Neutral Experience</span> </div></div></div> <div class='tightLt col span-1-3'> <div class='middle'> <div class="cell"><i class='sqLed middle sm yellow margRtSm '></i> </div><div class="cell"><span class='middle'>Average Interview</span> </div></div></div> </div> </div> <div class='description '> <div class='interviewReviewDetails truncateData' data-animate-after-less='true' data-click-anywhere='true' data-less-str='Show Less' data-more-str='Show More' data-truncate-toggle='true' data-truncate-words='70'> <p class="strong tightBot">Application</p> <p class='applicationDetails noMargVert notranslate'>I applied online. The process took 6 days. I interviewed at <tt class='i-emp'>Jane Street</tt> in June 2014.</p> <p class="strong tightBot">Interview</p> <p class='interviewDetails noMargTop notranslate truncateThis'>Applied online. Got contacted after two days and scheduled an phone interview. Lasted one hour. Asked quickly about my research and programming background. Then shifted to three mathematical problems. The last two questions seemed designed not to have a simple analytic answer and the interviewer asked to approach one of the problems intuitively and how confident I was about my answers. The interview ended with a few questions I asked about this position at Jane Street.</p> <p class="strong tightVert">Interview Questions</p> <div class='interviewQuestions margBot notranslate'> <ul class='undecorated'> <li> <span class='interviewQuestion noPadVert truncateThis ' data-truncate-words='70'>The last two questions revolved around the following game consisting of drawing two cards from a randomly shuffled deck and repeating the procedure until 2N cards have been drawn. You lose or win one dollar depending on various conditions. Given those conditions, which N gives the highest probability of winning at each step? What if the deck is built by drawing cards from another deck? How much should you get charged if this game is fair? &nbsp;</span> <a
